summary: PEC-G is a Brazilian government exchange programme, run by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Education with participating higher education institutions, that gives foreign students free places in full undergraduate degrees in all fields of knowledge, with no fees and no entrance exam. It is for nationals of participating (mainly developing) countries who live abroad. Students who do not yet know Portuguese apply to PEC-PLE as well, which gives a first Portuguese-language course in Brazil before the degree. Public Notice No. 22 of 25 March 2026 covers the selection for 2027 and allows up to 1,400 selected candidates.
eligibility_notes:
You must be a national of a country taking part in the programme, live abroad, and hold no Brazilian visa or residence permit except a tourist visa. You must not hold Brazilian nationality, including dual nationality or a right to it, and your father or mother must not be Brazilian. You must be at least 18 years old by 1 January 2027.

Education: you must show completion of a level equivalent to secondary school outside Brazil, with a global average of at least 60% across all subjects and at least 60% in the subject of your own official language. If you finish secondary school by the end of 2026 you may still apply and give the certificate when you enrol, if selected.

Portuguese (PEC-G only applicants): you must show, by the date in the call calendar, either the Celpe-Bras certificate or an intermediate-level certificate from a Portuguese course at a Guimaraes Rosa Institute unit. If you studied Portuguese as an official language through all of secondary school but have neither certificate, you need an average of at least 65% in Portuguese; this exception does not apply to people who finished secondary school in Timor-Leste or Equatorial Guinea. If you did not study Portuguese as an official language throughout secondary school and have no certificate, you must apply to PEC-PLE and PEC-G together and, if selected, take the Celpe-Bras exam in Brazil (optionally in the first half of 2027, compulsorily in the second half of 2027) after the Portuguese course. People who studied Portuguese throughout secondary school may apply only to PEC-G.

Financial support: you must hand in a Financial Responsibility Agreement signed by a financial sponsor who guarantees at least USD 300 per month for housing and living costs for the whole period of study, and you must sign a Commitment Agreement to follow the programme rules.

Not allowed to apply: Brazilian citizens (also those with a second nationality) and children of a Brazilian parent; candidates selected earlier who did not complete their first enrolment without a justification; students dismissed earlier from the programme; and candidates disqualified earlier for fraud or false documents. A PEC-PLE student who fails the Celpe-Bras after the maximum attempts allowed by the institution leaves the programme and cannot join PEC-G or apply again.
age_experience_notes: At least 18 years old by 1 January 2027. The call text read states no maximum age. A university page describes the programme as aimed at students aged 18 to 23, so the ages may be described that way elsewhere. No work experience is asked.
funding_summary: The place in a full-time undergraduate degree is free of tuition, and the student also gets medical, dental and pharmaceutical care through Brazil's public health system, and has final academic documents (diploma, course outlines, transcripts) legalised or apostilled free at the Brazilian embassy or consulate where they applied. In some cases there are grants and aid from the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the institution, but these are not guaranteed. The student's living costs are not paid by the programme: a financial sponsor must guarantee at least USD 300 a month for the entire period of study.
programmes_note: Places are in courses in all areas of knowledge, full-time classroom undergraduate degrees, with no entrance exam. Degree types are the bacharelado (average 4 to 5, sometimes 6 years), the licenciatura (teacher training, average 4 years) and the tecnologo (average 2 to 3 years). A PEC-G candidate may name up to two course options at up to two institutions: either one course option only (competing for all places in that course) or a specific institution, campus and intake semester (which limits the chance). Applicants to PEC-PLE and PEC-G together can only name the course, not the institution, for the degree. The list of institutions and courses, with degree type, campus, intake semester and number of places, is published on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs selection page.
institutions_note: Public (federal and state) and private Brazilian higher education institutions take part, together with their Portuguese-language courses for PEC-PLE. The list is published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs with each selection. The selection committee tries to spread selected students evenly over the institutions and regions of Brazil; the candidate does not choose freely. A PEC-PLE place and the later degree place may be in different institutions or cities, because not all degree institutions offer the Portuguese course.

summary.detail: Complete classroom undergraduate degree in Brazil (bacharelado, licenciatura or tecnologo), taught in Portuguese. Places in all areas of knowledge, no fees and no entrance exam. Direct PEC-G places start in 2027 for candidates who already hold the Celpe-Bras or equivalent; candidates who first take the PEC-PLE Portuguese course start the degree in 2028 once they pass the Celpe-Bras.
summary.source_text: free admission placements in undergraduate degree programs

requirements.text: Pre-registration: a legible scan of the complete secondary-school transcript (all subjects and all grades), with a simple translation into Portuguese, English, French or Spanish if not in one of these languages. One PDF of at most 10 MB, carrying the school's signatures and stamps or electronic validation code, or authenticated by the authority in the country of issue, or legalised as the embassy requires.

Pre-registration form data: overall secondary-school average (simple mean of all subject marks up to the date of pre-registration), chosen country and embassy or consulate, e-mail and phone number, and whether you rely on relatives or friends living in Brazil.
Original and copy of the secondary-school completion certificate or equivalent (shortlisted candidates, handed in at the embassy).
requirements.conditional_rule: if you finish secondary school by the end of 2026, a declaration that you are a likely graduate, and the certificate at enrolment

requirements.text: Original and copy of the secondary-school transcript listing all subjects and grades of all school years.
Original and copy of the applicant's birth certificate and of the parents' birth certificates (identification showing parentage, place and date of birth is accepted in the previous-year notice).
Original and copy of the Celpe-Bras certificate (any edition) or proof of an intermediate-level certificate from a Portuguese course of the Guimaraes Rosa Institute network.
requirements.conditional_rule: PEC-G only applicants who did not study Portuguese as the official language throughout secondary school; not needed if also applying to PEC-PLE

requirements.text: Commitment Agreement Form (TCI), prepared by the embassy in Portuguese, signed by the candidate in person.

Financial Responsibility Agreement (TRF) in Portuguese, signed by the sponsor with the signature notarised or legalised as the embassy decides. The sponsor attaches an official photo ID with signature and proof of net monthly income (for example tax return, employer letter, payslips or bank statements of the previous three months, or an employment contract). The total promised to the student must be at least USD 300 per month, and the signer's net monthly income must be at least three times the amount promised. Companies and organisations may sponsor; government bodies and international organisations may be excused from proof of income. Each sponsor signs a separate form.

Original medical certificate of physical and mental health, with the doctor's signature and stamp, saying whether the candidate is fit to study abroad and listing relevant conditions, regular medication and disabilities. Asked in the previous-year notice (carried over from the 2026 intake notice, not shown in the 2027 guide).

Documents other than the financial agreement must have a simple translation into Portuguese, English, French or Spanish unless already in one of those languages; the financial agreement itself must be in Portuguese. Embassies may check authenticity and ask for legalisation.

application_steps.title: Check the call and fill in the online pre-registration form
application_steps.detail: Public Notice No. 22 of 25 March 2026 opened the selection for 2027. Candidates completed the free online pre-registration form from 31 March to 9 May 2026, choosing the country and embassy or consulate where they register, giving e-mail and phone, the overall secondary-school average and the course options, and attaching the full secondary-school transcript as one PDF of at most 10 MB. Only the latest form counts if you filled it in twice. Pre-registration alone does not mean acceptance.

application_steps.title: Choose between PEC-G only and PEC-PLE with PEC-G
application_steps.detail: Apply to PEC-G alone if you hold the Celpe-Bras or an intermediate Portuguese certificate, or studied Portuguese as an official language throughout secondary school. Otherwise apply to PEC-PLE and PEC-G together; you take the Portuguese course in Brazil in 2027 and start the degree in 2028 if you pass the Celpe-Bras. You may name course options: for PEC-G alone, one course option or a specific institution, campus and semester; for both programmes, only the course.

application_steps.title: Hand in documents at the Brazilian embassy or consulate if shortlisted
application_steps.detail: The embassy or consulate you chose reviews pre-applications, and the shortlist was announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on 2 June 2026. Shortlisted candidates give originals and copies of the certificate, transcript, birth certificates and Portuguese proof (where needed), sign the Commitment Agreement, and hand in the signed and notarised Financial Responsibility Agreement with the sponsor's ID and proof of income, between 2 and 30 June 2026. Incomplete, altered or late documents are not accepted. The embassy then sends the application to the selection committee.

application_steps.title: A selection committee in Brazil assesses each application
application_steps.detail: The committee of staff from participating institutions met on 4 to 6 August 2026. In the previous-year notice it checks nationality, at least 60% secondary-school average, the sponsor's promised amount and income, and the Portuguese level; candidates are ranked by their grade average relative to the average of all candidates of their country and by Celpe-Bras level or Portuguese grade. It tries to give at least one place to each country and to each institution, and to spread students over regions. Where Celpe-Bras is offered in the candidate's country, holders of the certificate come first. A vacancy is not a right.

application_steps.title: Results come in several rounds on the Ministry website
application_steps.detail: Selected candidates in the first round and the waiting list were announced from 14 September 2026, with confirmations registered from 14 to 28 September. Lists of confirmed first-round candidates followed from 13 October, the second round from 26 October and the third round, if any, from 16 November 2026. Selected candidates must tell their embassy that they accept, withdraw or want a different remaining place, within the deadline the embassy sets. Withdrawn places go to the waiting list.

application_steps.title: Get information from the institution and obtain the student visa
application_steps.detail: Selected candidates receive enrolment, calendar and rules from the institution by e-mail and must follow the deadlines or be dropped from the programme. Selection does not guarantee entry into Brazil: you must apply for and get the right visa (the Ministry of Education page describes a temporary student visa) and keep your migration status regular. Candidates who do not enrol in time lose the place and must apply again. Based on the previous-year notice and a university page.

application_steps.title: Enrol with legalised documents; start the Portuguese course or degree
application_steps.detail: For first enrolment the student gives the institution the embassy introduction letter, apostilled or legalised birth and school documents, two copies of the commitment and financial agreements, proof of income, a medical certificate no more than three months old, the CPF tax number and passport with visa. Courses start from January 2027 (direct PEC-G and PEC-PLE) or January 2028 (degree after PEC-PLE and Celpe-Bras). A PEC-PLE student who does not pass the Celpe-Bras may be allowed to retry in later sittings, up to the institution's limit, and then leaves the programme.

application_steps.title: Finish the degree and go home
application_steps.detail: The programme expects students to return to their home country after finishing. The graduate is responsible for having the Brazilian degree recognised later. The financial agreement stays valid for the whole stay, with updated proof of the sponsor's income.
